npc_mey_shepherd.name: Mey
npc_mey_shepherd.look: A sturdy eleven-year-old girl with wind-reddened cheeks and a tangle of red-brown hair, a grey wool shawl over a green dress, bare legs, wooden clogs and a crook taller than she is.
npc_mey_shepherd.personality: Curious, brave and stubborn; asks 'why' about everything and believes in nothing she hasn't seen.
npc_mey_shepherd.values: her father, the flock, finding things out
npc_mey_shepherd.fears: the fog, losing her father on the hill
npc_mey_shepherd.authority: Minds the flock when her father is away.
npc_mey_shepherd.concerns: The fog comes down off the hill without warning; last spring her father was lost in it all night and they lost three ewes.

fog.text: When the fog comes down on the hill you can't tell one way from another; her father was lost in it last spring.
fog.line: When the fog comes down you can't tell up from down. Father was lost all night last spring.
fog.lead: The shepherds get lost on the hill when the fog comes down.

npc_mey_shepherd.persuaded_by: seeing it work with her own eyes
npc_mey_shepherd.style: Quick questions, one after another; sceptical, then delighted.

samples: Show me. I don't believe things I can't see.
Father says the fog's alive. I think it's just wet.
voice.habits: Asks why; wants to see things done; repeats new words.
voice.never: believes a thing just because she's told it
voice.greeting: Squints at you: 'You're not from the valley. Where are you from? Why?'

npc_mey_shepherd.likes: clever things, stories of far places

npc_orrin_shepherd.text: her father; brave but too proud to ask for help

tasks.doing: counting the sheep in the fold

superstition.text: Mey would be thrilled by anything uncanny and tell the whole valley.

npc_orrin_shepherd.name: Orrin
npc_orrin_shepherd.look: A lean, weather-beaten shepherd in his forties with a long face, a short dark beard going grey, a heavy brown wool cloak pinned at the shoulder, leather leggings, and a sling tucked in his belt.
npc_orrin_shepherd.personality: Quiet, proud and wary of strangers; superstitious about the hill and the fog.
npc_orrin_shepherd.values: his flock, his daughter, old ways
npc_orrin_shepherd.concerns: Fog season is coming; he keeps a lodestone his grandfather found, for luck, and doesn't know what it's for.

lodestone.text: Orrin keeps a lodestone his grandfather found: a black stone that pulls iron to it. He thinks it's lucky.
lodestone.line: That? Grandfather's stone. Pulls iron like a lover. Lucky, I'd say.
lodestone.lead: Orrin has a lodestone, a stone that pulls iron.

city.text: The city lets in strangers only when someone inside will vouch for them.
city.line: City? They let no stranger in now unless someone speaks for them.
city.lead: The city lets in strangers only if someone will speak for them.

npc_orrin_shepherd.persuaded_by: something that works on the hill, not talk
npc_orrin_shepherd.style: Few words, careful; touches the shrine stone for luck.

samples: The fog's not to be trifled with.
My grandfather's stone. Lucky. Or cursed. One of the two.
If that's a trick, it's a good one.
voice.habits: Watches before he speaks; touches wood or stone for luck.
voice.greeting: Nods, unsmiling: 'You're far from the road.'

goals: Bring the flock through fog season

npc_mey_shepherd.text: his daughter; too clever by half

tasks.doing: mending a hurdle outside the hut

superstition.text: Orrin fears anything uncanny: he'd call it witchcraft before he'd call it clever.
